rationale: This is a mechanical splice of two already-archived legs — the expense-mix ratio from "Expensing-Regime Cash Funding Floor" and the (oancf−dpc)/at leg from "Depreciation-Addback-Free Innovation Cash" — and since both conditioning legs proxy the same R&D-heaviness construct, it is a cosmetic variant rather than a new mechanism.

Identical in structure to the archived "Working-Capital-Invariant Innovation Realization" with only "−dpc" appended to the cash leg, which is a one-term tweak of an existing strong signal rather than a substantively different hypothesis, and stacking dpc, recch and invch subtractions on top of a margin leg that already re-adds recch/invch double-counts the same adjustments.

This is the archived "Accrual-Adjusted Innovation Margin" with xrd/sale subtracted from the second leg, and because that subtraction is mechanically the negative of the first leg the product partly cancels itself, making the economic interpretation (R&D productivity vs. R&D intensity) ambiguous rather than sharper.

The pairing of intangible-to-equity fragility with a declining amortization-recognition rate is an untested combination whose sign and expression are internally consistent, though both legs are recycled from archived signals and share intan−gdwl in numerator and denominator, so the mechanical overlap should be diagnosed if results look strong.

This is the archived "Intangible Equity Fragility with Accrual Support" with the accrual leg swapped for a negated cash-profitability leg, and since oancf−dpc scaled by assets is essentially a cash-profitability sort, the signal risks rediscovering the well-known profitability/distress effect conditioned on intangible intensity.

The archive already contains two versions of "capitalization migration plus weak cash" ("Nonoverlapping Capitalization Cash Failure", "R&D-to-Capitalized Migration Support"), and replacing the cash-trend leg with an addback-free cash level is an incremental leg swap rather than a diagnosis-driven redirection.
